summary: The school/religion context identifies the study verb, consistent with the inherited Arabic drs comparison. Source s versus glossary z is not evidence for a new root.
The negative Infectum-wa reports study in a past school situation; ʕal marks the topic of study. It does not establish a distinct religious-education sense.
A consonant-only lookup can miss the drs/drz spelling relation, but this is a lookup limitation rather than a correction to the published entry.

Jan 4.I/337 has unprefixed drəs-li, compatible with the inherited I L-series Preterit and the s/z variation already noted in round 1. It does not show the m-prefixed formation expected for the reader’s proposed II.

The adjacent mafono and eleven-year duration suggest a teacher’s career, but do not by themselves distinguish studying, working as a teacher, or a lexical teaching use of I. The English taught is machine-generated and cannot settle that ambiguity.

No new II stem, base pair, numbered teaching sense or published example is added on this low-confidence single token. The complete Turoyo evidence is retained in the editorial question rather than silently converted into I study.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Is s versus z an actual dialect distinction or a transcription convention?
Does ʕal productively introduce any study topic, or is this phrasing influenced by the school context? One attestation cannot decide.

At Jan 4.I/337, what is mafono in “i naqqa d mwaladno, mafono drəsli mede ḥḏaḥṣar (11) əšne”? Does drəsli mean studied or taught, and if taught is it an I use or an exceptional borrowed formation? The unprefixed form does not establish II.
